messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Sobol sequences
parts:
One issue that we have is that for a relatively small number of chains, randomly generating initial values on the (-a,a) interval in the unconstrained space doesn't necessarily create very overdispersed chains. One way to mitigate this would be to use a Sobol sequence

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sobol_sequence

of initial values on the (-a,a)^K cube. This is relatively easy to do in the RStan context via a function like this

stopifnot(require(rstan))
stopifnot(require(randtoolbox))

sobol_init <- function(object, chains, lower = -2, upper = -lower, ...) {
  stopifnot(is(object, "stanfit"))
  n <- get_num_upars(object)
  x <- qunif(sobol(n, dim = chains, init = TRUE, ...),
             min = lower, max = upper)
  param_dims <- object@.MISC$stan_fit_instance$param_dims()
  pars <- names(param_dims)
  skeleton <- rstan:::create_skeleton(pars, param_dims)
  return(apply(x, MARGIN = 2, FUN = function(y) {
    r <- relist(y, skeleton)
    r <- r[sapply(r, FUN = function(z) all(!is.na(z)))]
    constrain_pars(object, unlist(r))
  }))
}

which returns a list of length chains with overdispersed starting values in the constrained parameter space.

But it would be better if we could "upstream" this to Stan. There is BSD-licensed C++ code for Sobol sequences at

http://web.maths.unsw.edu.au/~fkuo/sobol/

but it would take some doing to rewrite the administrative stuff to not write to a file but instead keep the parameters x chains matrix in memory so that it can be used for starting values.

Sobol sequences would also be necessary if we ever want to do quasi Monte Carlo integration, which I have been talking about with Andrew for marginal maximum likelihood.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Sobol sequences
parts:
What does "overdispersed" mean in general? Is it that
you want pairwise distances to be very large while remaining
in the (-a,a)^K cube? And still presumably having some
degree of randomness?

Randomly generating each dimension on (-a,a) should
lead to fairly large expected distances between initial points,
but some of the dimensions may be close.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Sobol sequences
parts:
On Tuesday, February 25, 2014 2:07:14 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
What does "overdispersed" mean in general?

I just meant it in the BDA sense that you want the chains to start at overdispersed points so that Rhat and other convergence-related things are conservative. A low-discrepancy sequence is consistent with that sense of overdispersed because the points are constructed so that the chains are "evenly" distributed throughout the (-a,a)^K cube.

Is it that
you want pairwise distances to be very large while remaining
in the (-a,a)^K cube?  And still presumably having some
degree of randomness?
You can add randomness to it if you want, although it isn't so necessary. In addition to the distance thing, the columns (chains) are essentially uncorrelated, even without randomness.

Randomly generating each dimension on (-a,a) should
lead to fairly large expected distances between initial points,
but some of the dimensions may be close.

For a large K and a small number of chains, you don't have a great probability of "surrounding" a particular parameter with the starting values are just random.

In addition, if given a Sobol sequence on (0,1)^K, we could automatically search for an "a" such that the density, gradients, etc. are sane to start with on the (-a,a)^K cube.

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Sobol sequences
parts:
On Tuesday, February 25, 2014 3:03:30 PM UTC-5, Michael Betancourt wrote:
Yeah, I don’t think we’re anywhere near the point where the difference between
random, pseudorandom, and Sobel matters.  Even in high dimensions this isn’t
going to have a huge effect and you can argue that random is better anyways.

Mattering or better for what exactly? By construction, a Sobel is going to fill a hypercube more evenly than random or pseudorandom draws would. Are you saying that you don't think the additional evenness would create more overdispersion in the BDA sense of making it more challenging for multiple chains to converge and / or easier to discover multiple modes. I am not seeing why nondeterministic starting values would be essential for Stan, but if it is, you could pseudo-randomly scramble a Sobol sequence.

Ben

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Sobol sequences
parts:
On Feb 25, 2014, at 11:45 PM, Ben Goodrich <goodri...@gmail.com> wrote:

Are you saying that you don't think the additional evenness would create more overdispersion in the BDA sense of making it more challenging for multiple chains to converge and / or easier to discover multiple modes.

Yeah, I think it’ll be a small difference at best.  If there are features sensitive to such differences then
we have much, much bigger issues to deal with.
